title: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports
abstract: arXiv:2611.07486v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Mapping behavioral intelligence in malware analysis reports to ATT&CK techniques supports threat analysis and defense, but reliable identification remains challenging. Supporting evidence is often scattered across long, heterogeneous reports, while closely related techniques share behavioral cues and differ only in subtle but decisive details. While large language models (LLMs) can use external knowledge to interpret reports, they may assign techniques based on plausible associations rather than sufficient evidence. We present MEvince, a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework for report-level malware technique identification. Its core is a shared behavioral representation connecting report observations to technique definitions. translated_title: MEvince：面向恶意软件报告技术识别的知识约束大语言模型推理
translated_abstract: 将恶意软件分析报告中的行为情报映射到ATT&CK技术有助于威胁分析与防御，但可靠的技术识别仍然充满挑战。支持性证据往往散布在冗长且异构的报告之中，而相互关联的技术共享行为线索，仅在细微却起决定性作用的细节上有所差异。尽管大语言模型（LLM）能够利用外部知识来解读报告，但它们可能基于看似合理的关联而非充分的证据来指派技术。我们提出了MEvince，一个面向报告级恶意软件技术识别的知识约束LLM推理框架。其核心是连接报告观察结果与技术定义的共享行为表示。该表示通过对技术文档的智能体式挖掘构建而成，并支持两个在线阶段：1）原语引导的提取，利用行为原语对LLM提取的观察结果进行结构化处理……
tldr: MEvince提出了一种知识约束的LLM推理框架，通过构建连接报告观察结果与技术定义的共享行为表示，解决恶意软件报告中ATT&CK技术识别证据分散、技术界限细微的难题。
en_tdlr: MEvince is a knowledge-constrained LLM reasoning framework that reliably identifies ATT&CK techniques from malware reports by building a shared behavioral representation linking report observations to technique definitions.
